Can you advise on whether we should ask for H100-heavy pool, A100 balanced pool, or L4-first fleet with H100 fallback? Also curious about memory vs perf tradeoffs for our long-context paths and whether caching/prefixing changes the SKU decision.

Thanks for the details — quick technical readout and recommendations below (summary first, then rationale). I attached a draft "gpu-sku-scorecard" for your procurement team.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Primary pool: A100x2 (balanced) for the committed reserved capacity tier — gives predictable performance for 2k–4k typical contexts and good memory headroom for 8k spikes.
- Canary / burst: H100 instances sized for high-throughput and fast decode on burst windows where you need lower latency at scale. H100 for peak 95th when many simultaneous long-context sessions occur.
- Cost-efficient inference tier: L4 nodes for lower-cost, lower-latency short-chat QPS (shallow context). Use routing policy to prefer L4 for chat < 1k tokens.
- Operational hedge: start 60% A100 reserve / 25% L4 reserve / 15% H100 burst (adjustable after 1 quarter of telemetry).

Rationale and tradeoffs:
- Memory headroom: A100 (40/80GB vram options depending on SKU) provides a consistent memory footprint for >4k context models without extreme quantization. H100 gives more FP throughput and can reduce latency on long decode paths but is costlier per-token. L4 excels at cheap dense int8 inference for shorter contexts but struggles when KV cache size grows for 8k contexts.
- Quantization and model variants: For long-context summarization we recommend a 16-bit or mixed precision A100 path to avoid quality regressions; for short chat switch to int8 on L4. We can serve model variants and route by request profile automatically in the platform.
- Caching and prefix reuse: significant cost/latency wins if frequent prompt prefixes exist. Prefix/KV caching reduces H100 need for streaming long contexts — if CloudMetrics can pre-cache system prompts or heavy shared contexts, you can bias towards more A100/L4 and less H100.
- Autoscale & cold start: H100 instances should be used as a burst layer to keep committed costs down — they can be hot-swapped via our smart-routing policy when queueing is detected. Plan for a short warm-up window for H100-backed long-context sessions.

Operational playbook (concrete):
1) Deploy initial reserved pool: 12x A100 (80GB) + 20x L4 (per expected short-chat QPS) + 4x H100 for burst canary.
2) Configure routing rules: prefer L4 for requests <1k tokens; A100 for 1k–6k; H100 for >6k or when end-to-end latency rises above 220ms.
3) Enable KV prefix caching for conversational threads where conversation id is stable — expect ~30% token cost reduction in best cases.
4) Telemetry window: evaluate after 2 weeks of production traffic, then reweight reserve percentages.

Attachments: gpu-sku-scorecard-v1.pdf (PDF, 180KB) — contains a per-SKU score (cost/unit QPS, memory headroom, latency percentile) and the initial reserve/burst sizing spreadsheet.
